findings.title: No test cuts entity during a running session

findings.evidence: FieldFeatureTests.swift:22-35 is the only test whose drag crosses a entity, and it starts from `FieldSimulation(seed: 1, objects: [entity], count: 4, charges: 0, isFinished: true)`. FieldFeature.swift:57-62 `case .dragChanged(let point): if let last = state.trail.last { state.simulation.cut(along: [last, point]) }` has no test that checks the count or the objects after a live drag.
findings.failure_scenario: Delete `state.simulation.cut(along: [last, point])` at FieldFeature.swift:59. dragBuildsAndClearsTrail (lines 8-20) starts from FieldFeature.State(seed: 1), turns exhaustivity off, and only asserts the trail. dragAfterFinishedCountsNothing (lines 22-35) starts with isFinished: true and expects count == 4, which still holds when cutting never runs. tickAdvancesSimulation, restartResets and timerTicksAcrossSessions never send .dragChanged. LaunchFlowUITests only asserts the label reads 'Count: 0'. So the count never rises in a running session and every test still passes.
findings.fix: Add a test that starts a running session (`FieldSimulation(seed: 1, objects: [entity at (100,100), radius 20])`), sends .dragChanged at (50,100) and then (150,100), and expects count == 1 and the entity removed. Optionally add a hazard case that expects a lost charge.
findings.title: No test cuts entity during a running session
findings.verification_note: I read FieldFeatureTests.swift in full, FieldFeature.swift, and grepped UITests for count and cut. The only call to cut is at FieldFeature.swift:59. None of the five unit tests asserts that cutting changes anything in a running session. The trail test uses exhaustivity .off with no count check. The finished test passes whether cut runs or not, because the cut should do nothing after finished anyway. The UI test only checks the starting 'Count: 0'. So removing line 59 would leave the suite green, as the finding says. This is a test gap, not a runtime failure users hit, so I rated it under defect-narrow-trigger (major), which is the reviewer's severity.
